nodes.title: Algebraic G-isocrystals and sigma-conjugacy
nodes.statement: For connected reductive G/Q_p, k=F̄_p, L=Frac W(k), and Witt Frobenius σ, define B(G) as G(L) modulo b′=g⁻¹bσ(g). A G-isocrystal is an exact faithful Q_p-linear tensor functor Rep_Qp(G)→Isoc(k); its underlying L-valued fibre functor is isomorphic to scalar extension of the usual one. The functor attached to b sends (V,ρ) to (V⊗L,ρ(b)σ). Isomorphism classes identify with B(G); the automorphism functor of this tensor functor gives J_b. Finite rank is separate from the pinned isocrystal carrier; the full slope classification comes from R07.2, not its rank-one Mathlib special case.
hypotheses: Connected reductive G; algebraically closed residue field; rational, not integral, coefficients.
proofSteps: Use the pinned semilinear carrier and the tensor/representation dictionary supplied by reductive groups.
Trivialize the L-valued fibre functor; changing its trivialization changes b by sigma-conjugation. Frobenius-compatible tensor isomorphisms are exactly those conjugators.
Use Steinberg vanishing over L to justify the trivialization; record the tensor-descent primary-proof boundary G1.
acceptance: For GL_n the class is the isocrystal isomorphism class, not ordinary conjugacy.

nodes.title: Newton and Kottwitz invariants with the PEL sign
nodes.statement: For connected reductive G/Q_p, let D be the protorus with X*(D)=Q, π₁(G)=X_*(T)/coroot lattice with its Galois action, and N(G) the Galois-fixed geometric conjugacy classes of maps D→G. Define ν̄_G:B(G)→N(G) through rational slope decompositions in every representation, and κ_G:B(G)→π₁(G)_Γ. Both are functorial for group homomorphisms, and the image of ν̄ under abelianization equals κ⊗Q. For quasi-split G and a conjugacy class μ, B(G,−μ) means κ=−μ^natural and ν̄≤(−μ)^diamond in the dominant order (choose the dominant member before Galois averaging). This is a definition of the admissible locus, not a claim that every element occurs in a PEL special fibre. For the dual Dieudonné convention used below, BT slopes λ give ν weights −λ.
hypotheses: Fix a based root datum for dominance; μ and Galois action are specified.
proofSteps: Obtain the slope protorus grading from finite-dimensional isocrystals.
Use the algebraic fundamental group and the torus valuation map; extend by reductive-group descent as in RR Theorem 1.15.
Pin the duality and sign at the PEL comparison, and retain the primary general κ construction as G1.
acceptance: For GL_n, κ is v_p(det b) and ν̄ lists slopes; Σ of BT slopes λ_i gives κ=−Σλ_i with multiplicities.

nodes.title: Decent representatives, Newton Levi and J_b
nodes.statement: For quasi-split connected reductive G/Q_p and [b]∈B(G), choose a representative whose Newton map ν_b is rational and an integer s>0 with bσ(b)⋯σ^{s−1}(b)=(sν_b)(p) and sν_b integral. Then b∈G(L_s), M_b=Z_G(ν_b) is a Q_p-Levi and b is basic in M_b. The functor R↦{g∈G(L⊗_Qp R):g=bσ(g)b⁻¹} is represented by a reductive Q_p-group J_b, an inner form of M_b with descent cocycle Int(b). Fix an L_s-inner isomorphism ψ:J_b→M_b; transport stable classes to G geometrically. Changing b by sigma-conjugation changes J_b by an isomorphism canonical up to inner automorphism. The pair (M_b,[b] in B(M_b)) has a rational-conjugacy orbit independent of these choices. This last statement concerns classes in B(M_b), not rational conjugacy of every pair of actual representatives.
hypotheses: Quasi-split G for rational Newton Levi; decency integer can be enlarged.
proofSteps: Use Kottwitz §§4.3 and 6.2 to choose rational ν and solve the decency equation after finite unramified extension.
Descend the Levi by Int(b); centrality of the decency product makes the cocycle valid.
Identify the fixed functor with the descended group, and prove its independence using sigma-conjugators. The general representability argument is source boundary G1.
acceptance: If b is basic, M_b=G but J_b can be a nonsplit inner form.

nodes.title: PEL Dieudonné comparison and quasi-isogeny groups
nodes.statement: For unramified integral simple PEL data of type A or C (positive involution, split matrix B_p over unramified centres, self-dual O_B-stable lattice and positive h), use the dual of the usual contravariant rational Dieudonné module. It sends μ_{p∞} to L(−1), and a polarized BT group with B_p-action to a hermitian isocrystal with pairing valued in L(−1). The determinant condition cuts out the classes in B(G,−μ) that arise from these BT groups. For Σ of class b, rational quasi-isogenies preserving the action and polarization up to scalar identify with J_b(Q_p), canonically up to inner automorphism. Quasi-isogenies to another such BT group are exactly its Frobenius-compatible hermitian isocrystal isomorphisms.
hypotheses: The comparison is over F̄_p in the isogeny category; the pairing is nondegenerate and its similitude scalar is retained.
Type D is excluded. The membership condition does not assert nonemptiness of every Shimura Newton stratum.
proofSteps: Consume R07.2 Dieudonné full faithfulness and Cartier duality.
Dualize and track the Tate twist through the pairing: all λ become −λ.
Apply the concrete/tensor dictionary of Shin §4.2 and identify the automorphism functor.
acceptance: The multiplicative BT group has slope 1 before dualization and weight −1 after it; the étale group has weight 0.

nodes.title: Central leaves and completely slope-divisible families
nodes.statement: Fix the good-reduction PEL special fibre X_K over F̄_p and a polarized O_B-BT group Σ=⊕Σ_i with slopes 1≥λ_1>⋯>λ_r≥0. Its central leaf C_Σ is the reduced locus where the geometric BT group with all additional structures is isomorphic to Σ, inside the Newton stratum with class b. It is smooth and closed in that stratum, not necessarily closed in X_K. A BT group H is completely slope divisible if it has a filtration whose graded pieces have slopes λ_i and, for one common s>0, p^{−sλ_i}F^s is an isomorphism on each graded piece and induces the required isogenies on the filtered pieces; use the exact filtration/isogeny condition of Mantovan §3. For a completely slope-divisible Σ, H=A[p∞]|C_Σ has this filtration, equivariant for O_B, and the polarization pairs grade i with the complementary slope 1−λ_i. Over a perfect field the filtration splits; it need not split over C_Σ.
hypotheses: Unramified integral PEL type A or C, hyperspecial level at p and neat prime-to-p level; reduced schemes, all geometric fibres.
Choose Σ satisfying the determinant condition.
proofSteps: Use the PEL representable smooth model and its universal BT group.
Apply the central-leaf and slope-filtration results quoted in Mantovan §3; retain their primary proof boundary G2.
Morphisms preserve slopes, and duality exchanges λ and 1−λ; this gives the inherited action and graded pairings.
acceptance: Fixing an isogeny class defines the Newton stratum; fixing an isomorphism class defines the finer central leaf.

nodes.title: Finite-level Igusa moduli and deck groups
nodes.statement: For m≥1 define Ig_{K^p,m} over C_{Σ,K^p} by O_B-equivariant isomorphisms j_i:Σ_i[p^m]→gr_i(A[p∞])[p^m], compatible with the graded polarization up to one common unit modulo p^m, which extend étale locally to every higher truncation. With Γ_b=Aut_O_B,λ(Σ)⊂J_b(Q_p) and U_p(m)=ker(Γ_b→Aut(Σ[p^m])), this functor is a finite étale Γ_b/U_p(m)-torsor over the leaf. It is smooth, finite type and usually nonproper. Higher level maps are finite étale and are restriction of the j_i. The U_p(m) form a basis of compact open subgroups of Γ_b. Ig_∞ denotes the inverse system and its inverse-limit geometric points, not a new finite-type scheme.
hypotheses: The central leaf and slope-divisible Σ of the preceding target; m≥1.
The lifting condition is part of the moduli problem; arbitrary truncated isomorphisms are not substituted for it.
proofSteps: Represent the liftable truncation trivializations and impose the closed O_B and polarization conditions.
Use formal rigidity of isoclinic groups to transport fibre trivializations over completed local rings, as in Mantovan Proposition 4.
The compact integral automorphism group gives the deck quotient, whose action is free and transitive on every fibre; primary liftability/rigidity proof inputs remain G2.
acceptance: The torsor has degree |Γ_b/U_p(m)|; its finite étaleness does not make the leaf proper.

nodes.title: The slope-separated quasi-isogeny monoid
nodes.statement: Order the BT slopes decreasingly. For δ∈J_b(Q_p) with δ⁻¹ an integral isogeny, let e_i be the least integer such that ker δ_i⁻¹⊂Σ_i[p^{e_i}], and f_i the largest integer such that Σ_i[p^{f_i}]⊂ker δ_i⁻¹. Define S_b by these isogeny conditions and f_{i−1}≥e_i for i≥2. Kernel gluing gives δ:Ig_{K^p,m}→Ig_{K^p,m−e_1} for m≥e_1 and compatible prime-to-p Hecke maps. Γ_b, p⁻¹ and fr^{−s} lie in S_b, where fr^{−s} acts with valuations −sλ_i; J_b(Q_p)=⟨S_b,p,fr^s⟩. This is an action of a monoid on a level system; it does not assert geometric actions of arbitrary J_b-elements at a fixed level.
hypotheses: Σ split into completely slope-divisible components with additional structures; common s integral on all slopes.
proofSteps: Glue the finite flat subgroup with the prescribed graded kernels using f_{i−1}≥e_i, then take the abelian quotient and its induced structures.
Functoriality of quotients yields the monoid law after enough level has been chosen.
Negative scalar and Frobenius powers put each quasi-isogeny into this cone; retain the general kernel-gluing proof boundary G2.
acceptance: For δ=p⁻¹, all e_i=f_i=1; for fr^{−s}, e_i=f_i=sλ_i, in decreasing order.

nodes.title: Rational Igusa cohomology and the full group action
nodes.statement: For ℓ≠p and an algebraic representation ξ of G, let L_ξ be its rational ℓ-adic coefficient system on the PEL model and its pullback to finite Igusa varieties. Define H_c^k(Ig_b,L_ξ)=colim_{K^p,m}H_c^k(Ig_{K^p,m},L_ξ), using finite étale level pullbacks. The S_b×G(A_f^p) action extends uniquely to J_b(Q_p)×G(A_f^p), since p⁻¹ and fr^{−s} act invertibly on rational cohomology. These are smooth admissible representations, vanish for k>2dim C_Σ, and their K^p×U_p(m) invariants equal finite-level cohomology. Set [H_c]=Σ_k(−1)^k[H_c^k], and evaluate test functions by Haar integration with compatible quotient measures. This uses finite-dimensional invariant spaces, not finite-dimensionality of the full infinite-level representation.
hypotheses: Neat level, ℓ≠p, rational ℓ-adic coefficients, and ξ algebraic.
Choose an identification Q̄_ℓ≅C when discussing complex characters.
proofSteps: Consume the algebraic étale finite-level cohomology and six operations supplier.
Mantovan Lemma 6 identifies the central actions with level projection and Frobenius; rational cohomology inverts both.
Admissibility follows by exact averaging for the finite deck quotient and the level-invariant identity; dimension gives the bounded alternating sum.
acceptance: Changing the Haar measure by a scalar changes the integrated characteristic-function trace by that scalar.

nodes.title: A finite-field model compatible with the central Frobenius action
nodes.statement: After enlarging a common decency integer s to contain the reflex residue field, each finite Igusa level admits a model J_{K^p,m}/F_{p^s} whose absolute p^s-Frobenius, transported to F̄_p and interpreted with the level-transition identifications, is fr^{−s}. For a finite family of S_b-Hecke correspondences, enlarge the field and source levels so the schemes, both legs and coefficient lifts descend to one finite field. This is a descent theorem, stronger than the elementary fact that a finite-type F̄_p-scheme has some finite-field model.
hypotheses: Use the central fr^{−s} defined by the fixed slope-divisible Σ, and compatible levels and polarization.
proofSteps: Mantovan Lemma 6 compares quotient-by-Frobenius with absolute Frobenius and level projection.
Construct the compatible descent datum by the isomorphism p^{−sλ_i}F^s on each slope piece.
Verify effectivity and coefficient compatibility; Shin Lemma 6.3 cites the detailed thesis §2.3, which is the precise unread primary boundary G3.

nodes.statement: Let PIC be the set of B-linear polarized abelian varieties z=(A,λ,ι) over F̄_p up to B-linear quasi-isogeny carrying λ to a positive rational multiple, whose prime-to-p hermitian Tate module is V⊗A_f^p and whose polarized rational BT group is Σ up to quasi-isogeny. A fixed point of a coset operator determines a rational acceptable element a∈H_z(Q), modulo rational conjugacy at this intermediate orbit step. For the final effective-triple parameter set, define FPAV to consist instead of a near-equivalence class of z and an H_z(A)-conjugacy class [a] of an acceptable rational a. Near equivalence requires isometry of the structured Tate spaces at every ℓ≠p and of the polarized rational BT modules at p, not merely the same unpolarized Newton polygon.

nodes.title: Finite-field Tate full faithfulness and Honda classification
nodes.statement: For abelian varieties A,B over F_q and ℓ≠p, Hom_Fq(A,B)⊗Z_ℓ≅Hom_Gal(T_ℓA,T_ℓB). If K=Q(π) and D=End_Fq^0(A), then Z(D)=K; inv_v D is 1/2 at real places, 0 at complex places and finite places away from p, and [K_v:Q_p]v(π)/v(q) modulo Z at v|p. If e is the index of D, then 2dim A=e[K:Q]. Honda existence, including the real Weil-number cases, is a separate proof input from Tate full faithfulness.

nodes.title: Effective p-adic types with common-refinement equivalence
nodes.statement: For a CM field or totally real field M with involution c, a p-adic type is an effective rational divisor η on its p-places such that η+cη=[p], where [p] has coefficient e(x/p). A simple type is minimal under descent through involution-preserving subfields. A type with multiplicities is (M=∏M_t,η,(n_t)_{t},κ:F→M), with n_t positive integers and κ compatible with involutions. Pullback to M′ multiplies η_x by e(y/x) at y|x; equal simple factors are combined by adding n_t. Identify two data only after a common refinement respecting η, multiplicities and κ, and select their unique minimal representative. The associated BT slopes are η_x/e(x/p). This normalized divisor records a geometric isogeny class over F̄_p after a finite field of definition and all endomorphisms have been chosen; it is not merely a fixed-F_q Frobenius polynomial.

nodes.statement: B-linear abelian varieties over F̄_p up to B-linear isogeny correspond to the minimal effective p-adic types with multiplicities and compatible κ, subject to the Morita dimensions of B. nodes.title: Igusa triples, centralizer isocrystals and the effective obstruction
nodes.statement: An Igusa triple of type b is (γ_0;γ,δ), where γ_0∈G(Q) is semisimple and R-elliptic, γ∈G(A_f^p) is geometrically conjugate to γ_0 place by place, and δ∈J_b(Q_p) is acceptable and geometrically conjugate to γ_0 through the fixed inner identification. Identify γ_0 by rational stable conjugacy, γ by ordinary G(A_f^p)-conjugacy, and δ by ordinary J_b(Q_p)-conjugacy. Write I_0=Z_G(γ_0), connected for these type A/C groups with simply connected derived group, and I_δ=Z_{J_b}(δ), its p-adic inner form. Transport the hermitian isocrystal while identifying γ_0 with δ to obtain a basic b_δ∈B((I_0)_Qp). Define α_p=κ_{I_0}(b_δ), α_v from the rational-class cocycle for γ_v at v≠p,∞, and α_∞ from μ on an elliptic real torus. For this elliptic I_0 set K(I_0/Q)=(⋂_v Z(Î_0)^{Γ_v}Z(Ĝ))/Z(Ĝ). Extend the local characters to Z(Î_0)^{Γ_v}Z(Ĝ), with restrictions −μ on Z(Ĝ) at p, +μ at infinity and zero elsewhere. Their product descends to α∈K(I_0/Q)^D. The triple is effective iff α=1. Realize M_H as a Q_p-Levi of H with a cocharacter ν_{M_H} mapping geometrically to ν_b; choose compatible L-morphisms and fix representatives of the finite coset set Out(H,s,η)/Out_G(M_H,s_H,η_H), giving embeddings I(M_H,H). For each effective stable pair there is a unique embedding coset, up to the permitted automorphism of the Levi datum, carrying its M_H-class to the given H-class. Its elements are acceptable for every embedded cocharacter iν_{M_H}. Empty effective Levi sets contribute zero.

nodes.title: Acceptable Levi functions, ordinary orbital integrals and normalized Jacquet modules

Its stable version is SO_g(φ̃)=δ_{P(ν)}(m)⁻¹SO_m(φ) when g is stably conjugate to an acceptable m, and zero otherwise. For irreducible admissible π, tr π(φ̃)=tr J_{P(ν)^op}^{G_0}(π)(φ), where J_P=Jac_P⊗δ_P^{−1/2}. This is the specified normalized lift, including the full δ_P⁻¹ orbital factor; it is not arbitrary parabolic induction.

Choose its ordinary endoscopic transfer φ_{M_H} to M_H supported on the intersection of the open iν_{M_H}-acceptable cones, using Shin’s cutoff argument; its regular orbital integrals retain matching. For each i∈I(M_H,H), multiply by δ_{P(iν_{M_H})}^{−1/2} and apply the acceptable-Levi lift to H, obtaining φ̃_{M_H,i}. Define h_p^H=Σ_{M_H}Σ_i c_{M_H}φ̃_{M_H,i}; use zero when the effective set is empty. Its stable orbital integral at every (G,H)-regular semisimple γ_H equals the κ-weighted O_p factor of prestabilization for matching effective data, and vanishes for ineffective/nonmatching classes. nodes.statement: Let Π_1,Π_2 be finite virtual complex smooth admissible representations of G(A_f^p)×J_b(Q_p), or the finite families of irreducible constituents visible after fixing the other test functions and a p-level. If their traces agree for every acceptable function, they agree for every compactly supported locally constant function. More locally, for fixed φ suppose the difference on φ^(N) is Σ_{j=1}^r c_j z_j^{−N}, where z_j are distinct nonzero eigenvalues of the central fr^s after grouping constituents with equal eigenvalues. If it vanishes for every sufficiently large integer N, then all c_j vanish and the difference at N=0 vanishes. No diagonalizability of a central action on arbitrary extensions is assumed: compute traces in the finite Grothendieck decomposition, where the central element acts by scalars on irreducibles.
